clue.text: Like normal, since Reading University's broken into

parts.note: 'since' in the sense 'because' can be AS

indicators.note: the word for reading is split open so that another letter can be put inside it

parts.note: a perusal is a reading of something
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Someone claims a break-in at Reading University was nothing out of the ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading looks like the town with its university, but it is a common noun here. 'broken into' puts U inside PERUSAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means 'in the customary way', the same idea as behaving in the normal fashion.

clue.text: Pleasantly old-fashioned queen is not speaking informally

parts.note: queen gives QU
colloquial speech contracts 'is not' to ain't

explanation.surface: A queen who sounds charmingly dated drops into casual slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Quaint describes something attractively unusual in an antique, olde-worlde way.

clue.text: Article healer kept among produce?

indicators.note: the two short pieces are held inside the letters of the verb, split around them

parts.note: to produce something is to make it
an is the indefinite article in grammar
DR, short for doctor, is someone who heals

explanation.surface: A grammatical article and a doctor are stored away with the farm produce.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also reads as a description: the mandrake root was prized by old herbalists as medicine, a healing plant among a crop.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandrake is a plant whose root was used in folk medicine, so it is a crop with curative powers.

clue.text: Not characteristic of contrary Baker, going into Europe

indicators.note: contrary means the other way round, so the whole assembly is read backwards
one piece enters the other, sitting within its letters

parts.note: EU is the European Union
a kiln is something that bakes pottery or bricks

explanation.surface: Some contrary character called Baker joins Europe, quite out of character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going into' and 'contrary' both act; the turned assembly reads EKILNU backwards. Baker looks like a surname but is something that bakes.
explanation.definitionFit: If something is unlike a person, it is not typical of them, as in 'it's unlike her to be late'.

clue.text: Hang about with transfer

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: to hang in the air is to hover
with can mean together with, AND

explanation.surface: Someone is told to linger around and help with a transfer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hang about' reads as the phrase meaning wait, but 'about' is the container signal here.
explanation.definitionFit: A handover is the act of passing something or someone from one party to another.

clue.text: Judge a gym trick

parts.note: PE, physical education, is gym class at school

explanation.surface: A judge is caught pulling a stunt at the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: PE (physical education) is the British school name for gym lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: A jape is a prank or practical joke.

clue.text: Kissing cousin played with a lot

indicators.note: letters that are played with are fiddled about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A kissing cousin is someone you played with a great deal as a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kissing cousin' is a set phrase, but here 'Kissing' is the definition and 'cousin' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Osculation is the formal or jocular word for the act of kissing.

clue.text: Endless shifting axis: thin blue line, ultimately

indicators.note: shifting letters move about into a new order
ultimately points to the very end of the word that follows it

explanation.surface: The thin blue line of police seems endlessly shifting along some axis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifting' rearranges AXISTHINBLUE into INEXHAUSTIBL; the last letter of line adds E. The thin blue line is a British nickname for the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that cannot be used up has no end to its supply.

clue.text: Speak of elderliness and dismiss hero

indicators.note: spoken out, the two words run together give the sound needed

parts.note: elderliness is old age; to dismiss someone from a job is to axe them

explanation.surface: Talk of being too old and fire the champion.
explanation.walkthrough: AGE + AXE said together gives the sound of the Greek hero's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ajax was one of the great Greek warriors of the Trojan War in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Video feature attracted an audience of 500 being shown to the back

indicators.note: the named letter is sent from its place to the end of the word

parts.note: to draw in a crowd is to attract one, past tense drew in
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A video feature drew in an audience of five hundred when screened at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: The move takes the D at the front of DREWIN and puts it at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Rewind is a function on a video player that runs the tape backwards.

clue.text: Bad person always embracing bad idol

indicators.note: one word holds another within its letters as in a hug

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters are spoilt and reformed in a new order

explanation.surface: A wicked person always clings to a false idol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' and 'embracing' do the work; the scrambled idol becomes ILDO before going in.
explanation.definitionFit: An evildoer is a wrongdoer, someone who commits wicked acts.

clue.text: It's obvious hosting street club provides refreshment for birds

indicators.note: the exclamation holds the other pieces inside it, as a host takes in guests

parts.note: duh is the slang exclamation meaning that is obvious
a bat is a club used in sport

explanation.surface: Evidently a street club lays on refreshments for its feathered visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: Birds clean their feathers by rolling in dry earth, which is the refreshment meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparrows and other birds roll in loose earth to clean their plumage, a dry-earth wash.

clue.text: Fabulous language of slurring singer in jumpsuit?

definitions.meaning: fabulous here means belonging to fable, the tongue of the elf folk in fantasy
a jokey adjective for the style of the mumbling rock-and-roll King in his white jumpsuit

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what tongue the mumbling singer in the jumpsuit is speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: Fabulous means 'of fable', not marvellous. The second sense adds -ISH to the singer's name, as in Presley-like.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolkien invented tongues for his elves, and the word also means resembling Presley's slurred style.

clue.text: Mock editor holding eatery up, looking embarrassed

indicators.note: the outer pieces hold the turned word between them

parts.note: mock means fake, a sham

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: a cafe is a small eatery

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor, ridiculed for holding up a restaurant, looks sheepish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads the eatery backwards as EFAC, since this is a down entry; 'holding' places it in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Shamefaced means showing embarrassment or guilt in one's expression.

clue.text: Recycling leader cut temporary increase in vague case of inertia

indicators.note: in signals one piece sitting inside the other

parts.note: something vague is unclear

indicators.note: cut means the last letter is chopped off

parts.note: a bulge is a brief rise, as in a population bulge

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A recycling chief cut back on a short-term spike in some woolly instance of idleness.
explanation.walkthrough: Uncle Bulgaria is the elder who leads the Wombles, furry British children's TV characters who recycle litter. 'cut', 'in' and 'case of' all act.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of the Wombles, whose whole business is recycling rubbish found on Wimbledon Common.

clue.text: Watch host endlessly rambling here?

indicators.note: rambling words wander about, so the letters are mixed up
endlessly means the final letter of the word is lost

explanation.surface: A viewer suggests watching a presenter who goes on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts host to HOS, and 'rambling' mixes WATCHHOS. As a whole the clue describes a talk show.
explanation.definitionFit: A talk show is a TV programme where a presenter chats with guests, a place to see one ramble on.

clue.text: Not at all restricted by transparent stuff, with time for openness

indicators.note: restricted by means held inside the other word

parts.note: glass is see-through material
not at all can be the flat answer no

explanation.surface: With time, being hemmed in by something clear gives way to openness.
explanation.walkthrough: Glasnost was the Soviet policy of openness under Gorbachev.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian word for the 1980s Soviet policy of transparency in government.

clue.text: Blur former line crossed by a storehouse

indicators.note: the line runs across inside the other pieces

parts.note: a barn is a farm storehouse

explanation.surface: A one-time line of the band Blur is cut through by a warehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Blur is a British band; Damon Albarn co-founded it. 'former' means one who formed it, not 'previous'.
explanation.definitionFit: Damon Albarn is the singer who founded the 1990s Britpop band.

clue.text: Disputes that in France are stopping informer's difficult getaway

indicators.note: stopping means plugging up the inside of the other word

parts.note: a nark is slang for a police informer
rows are quarrels or disputes
que is French for that
an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A

explanation.surface: Quarrels in France hold up the getaway of a police informant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopping' plugs the informer with the other pieces. The 's of informer's is a link word, not a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A close shave or near miss, an escape only just achieved.

clue.text: Trek in SA may be directed here?

definitions.text: Trek in SA may be directed here?

indicators.note: letters that are directed are ordered about into a new sequence

explanation.surface: A tourist wonders whether a South African trek might be routed this way.
explanation.walkthrough: SA is South Africa. Transkei was a nominally independent black homeland within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Transkei was a homeland region in the south-east of South Africa, a place a trek could be aimed at.

clue.text: See 19
Bra flies apart, which may affect shape of chest?

definitions.text: which may affect shape of chest?

indicators.note: flying apart breaks the letters up and lets them settle in a new order

explanation.surface: A bra bursting open certainly alters the look of one's bust.
explanation.walkthrough: Bra looks like the definition area, but chest means the ribcage.
explanation.definitionFit: The lower rib pairs not joined directly to the breastbone form part of the ribcage's shape.

clue.text: Excuse me from regular instalments in cash terms

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, every second one, from the words

explanation.surface: Pardon me for asking about the regular payment plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A throat-clearing sound used to attract attention politely or show disapproval.

clue.text: Attach universal film certificate to back nutty confection?

indicators.note: back means the whole assembly is read in reverse

parts.note: to tag something on is to attach it
U is the British film rating for universal, suitable for all
to as in 'the door was to' can mean on, closed or attached

explanation.surface: Stick a universal film rating on the back of a nutty sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TAG + U + ON into the answer. U is the British certificate for films suitable for all ages.
explanation.definitionFit: A chewy sweet made with honey, sugar and nuts such as almonds.

clue.text: Unknown character central to story, faceless nobody

parts.note: in algebra x, y and z are the unknowns

indicators.note: losing its face means the first letter is taken off

parts.note: the hero is the main figure in a story

explanation.surface: An anonymous figure at the heart of the tale is a faceless nonentity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central to story' looks like a pick of the middle letter of story; it is part of the definition of hero.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonentity, a person of no importance, is often called a nothing or a cipher.

clue.text: He should have gone before public speaker with twisted heart!

indicators.note: the two letters at the very middle are turned about, swapping places

parts.note: overt means open, public
a sayer is one who speaks

explanation.surface: A public orator has a warped character, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: In OVERTSAYER the central TS is twisted into ST. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: One who stays beyond the permitted time, especially past a visa's expiry, ought to have left earlier.
